purpose: Settle the distinction raised in the Phase 82 GPU-track audit: aggregate offload-rate equality across capacity arms had been measured, but complete per-task action-sequence equality had not. This probe compares the admitted pilot cells' per-step action arrays element-wise across all capacity arms within each fleet seed.
method: For each fleet seed {0,1,2}, the published per-step.npz of cap-2.5 was compared element-wise against cap-1.5, cap-1.0, and cap-0.75 on three arrays: veh_action (3600 x 2488 int8), veh_best_rsu (int16), veh_best_v2v (int16). Inputs are the hash-verified outputs of the 12 admitted pilot cells under data/vec-fresh/capacity-pilot/.
conclusion: Within every fleet seed, the complete per-second per-vehicle-slot action sequences, including chosen RSU and V2V targets, are bit-identical across all four capacity arms. The capacity-invariance finding holds at the keyed action level, not only at the aggregate-rate level.
interpretation_limits: Exploratory, owner_approved_candidate; descriptive and non-causal; scope is the pilot grid (one actor, one trace, four capacity levels, three seeds).
Identity of action sequences does not by itself establish why the policy is capacity-insensitive; observation-content analysis remains future work.
The arrays compared are the admitted published artifacts; this probe wrote nothing and admitted nothing.
